subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency — next steps

Subject: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency — next steps

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps:

- Requirement recap: NordBank needs EU data residency for all production data; APAC usage is lower priority but may be needed later. You flagged that no data should leave the EU and cross-region routing is a blocker for your compliance team.
- Deployment modes discussed: Hosted API (EU-only region pinning), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in an EU region with stronger isolation), and Private (VPC/on-prem) for full network control & KMS/HSM integration.
- Open questions for you: 1) Is EU-only Hosted API sufficient if we guarantee EU-only data plane + customer-managed KMS? 2) Would you prefer Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed resources in your VPC) or Private VPC/on-prem for the initial rollout? 3) Any procurement timeline or PO requirements we should be aware of?

I attached a short deployment-options PDF that lays out the tradeoffs (redwood-deployment-options.pdf). Next suggested step: a 30–45 minute architecture review with our Solutions Engineering team to validate network/KMS needs and finalize the recommended path. Are you available for a review next Tue/Wed (Jul 20/21) morning CET?

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (summary + decision matrix)

From: Lena Schultz <lena.schultz@nordbank.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@nordbank.com>
Date: 2027-07-18T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency — next steps

Thanks Aditya — good summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- EU-only is a hard requirement for production customer data. We cannot have any cross-region routing or replication that places customer PII outside the EU.
- For crypto/key management, we need customer-managed keys (BYOK) and support for our HSM solution.
- Compliance: please include SOC 2 evidence and any relevant penetration test summaries.

Given that, our security team prefers to see either: 1) a Dedicated deployment with strong network isolation in an EU region and guaranteed no egress outside the EU; or 2) Private VPC/on-prem where we control the VPC and keys. Hosted API with region pinning may be acceptable, but only if you can provide written guarantees that the data plane endpoints and backups remain within the EU and we can use our KMS.

Procurement: we typically need an initial proposal and estimated TCO for Dedicated vs Private (including implementation timeline). Can you include ballpark pricing and a target SLA for latency and uptime for the Dedicated option?

Subject: Re: Deployment mode & EU/APAC data residency — next steps

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear requirements. I wanted to follow up with specific implementation notes and the attachments we discussed (soc2-summary.pdf). High level:

1) Hosted API (EU-only region pinning)
   - We can pin customer traffic to EU data plane endpoints (currently: eu-west-1 and eu-central-1).
   - By default, we do not replicate production data outside the pinned region. We can add a contractual data residency clause and Technical Addendum that prohibits cross-region routing for your account.
   - BYOK/KMS: hosted option supports customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; we can support keys that restrict decryption to EU HSM zones.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity in EU)
   - Dedicated pools run in your chosen EU region and are isolated at the GPU-pool level; network egress can be restricted via VPC peering and strict routing rules.
   - SLA and latency commitments can be included in the Dedicated contract; pricing is a committed monthly spend (we'll provide bands).

3) Private VPC / On-prem
   - Full control over networking and keys. We provide a Private control plane and data plane nodes that run inside your VPC or on-prem cluster; logs and telemetry can be forwarded to your SIEM.
   - This option takes longer to stand up (typical 6–10 weeks depending on procurement and network setup).

A couple of notes on cross-region routing and backups: we can disable automatic cross-region replicas and ensure snapshots remain within the EU region for Dedicated and Hosted pinned accounts. For Private deployments, snapshot behavior is under your control.

I attached our SOC 2 summary and a short architecture diagram in the deployment PDF. Next steps I recommend:
- Confirm preferred deployment model (Hosted pinned / Dedicated EU / Private VPC).
- Schedule a 45-minute architecture review with your security and network teams — we can walk through KMS key flow and routing controls.
- I'll prepare a draft TCO/price band for Dedicated vs Private once you confirm expected qps and peak token volume.

Proposed times for the architecture review: Tue Jul 20 09:00–11:00 CET or Wed Jul 21 09:00–11:00 CET. Which works best?

Best,
